question: Jyotirao Govindrao Phule popularly known as Jyotiba founded the Satya-Shodhak in ________ for the cause of the oppressed.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1873**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Jyotirao Govindrao Phule, commonly known as Jyotiba, founded the **Satya Shodhak Samaj** in 1873.
 
• The organization was established in **Maharashtra, India**, to promote social equality and fight against the caste system.
 
• The primary aim of the Satya Shodhak Samaj was to **liberate the oppressed classes** from exploitation and discrimination.
 
• Jyotiba Phule and his wife, Savitribai Phule, were pioneers in promoting **education for women and lower castes** through this organization.
 
• The Samaj advocated for **rational thinking, social reform, and the abolition of social hierarchy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jyotirao Phule**

 
 
• Jyotirao Phule was born on 11 April 1827 in Pune, Maharashtra.
 
• He is recognized as a prominent social reformer and activist against the caste system in India.
 
• He was also a notable writer and thinker who authored several books advocating social reform.
 
 
 
• **Savitribai Phule**
 
 
• Savitribai Phule was the wife of Jyotirao Phule and a leading figure in women’s education in India.
 
• She established the first girls' school in Pune in 1848, alongside her husband.
 
• Savitribai Phule is considered one of the first female teachers in India.
 
 
 
• **Satya Shodhak Samaj**
 
 
• The organization was open to all castes and aimed at promoting social unity and equality.
 
• It focused on eradicating the evils of untouchability and caste discrimination.
 
• The Samaj also worked towards the economic upliftment of the oppressed classes.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of Jyotirao Phule**
 
 
• Jyotirao Phule's work laid the foundation for the anti-caste movement in India.
 
• He is often referred to as the "Father of Indian Social Revolution."
 
• His efforts have had a lasting impact on the social structure and reform movements in India.
